$comment: Known high/critical npm audit findings, pinned so the gate can fail on anything NEW.
This is NOT a suppression: each entry names the package, why it is not fixed yet, and a date
by which it must be re-triaged. Past that date the gate fails, forcing a decision rather than
letting the backlog age silently — which is what `|| true` did for as long as it was there.
Removing an entry is the goal; adding one requires a reason.

allowed.reason: Pinned to 16.0.10 exactly. The advisories resolve in 16.2.x, which is outside the stated dependency range and pulls a framework upgrade — a tracked upgrade, not an audit fix.
Inherited libvips CVEs. The fix requires next@16.2.12 via npm audit fix --force, so it is blocked behind the same framework upgrade.
Transitive through the Next build toolchain; not reachable at runtime and not upgradable independently of Next.
Transitive dev/build-time dependency, not part of any request path in the shipped server.
Transitive through the schema validation stack; no direct import.
Transitive through the vendored Open WebUI SPA bundle, which is a prebuilt third-party artifact.
